production_guardrails.master_staging_guardrail: Preserve the source property exactly. Do not alter architecture, room geometry, walls, ceiling, flooring, windows, doors, openings, columns, beams, stairs, fireplaces, niches, built-ins, fixed cabinetry, countertops, baseboards, permanent finishes, or room dimensions. Preserve the exact camera position, crop, field of view, perspective, exterior view, daylight direction, time-of-day impression, and visible permanent lighting. Do not add permanent construction, new windows, doors, openings, wall panels, ceiling treatments, fixed shelving, or architectural lighting. Add only realistically scaled movable furniture and decor appropriate to the room's existing function. Keep circulation paths clear. Avoid duplicate, floating, fused, or distorted objects, people, pets, logos, watermarks, readable text, and generated calligraphy.
production_guardrails.master_no_furniture_guardrail: Remove all clearly movable furniture, rugs, plants, freestanding decor, personal objects, artwork, freestanding lighting, TVs and media devices. Semi-fixed policy: keep curtains, blinds, curtain rods and tracks; keep wall-mounted mirrors; keep ceiling fans; keep radiators, HVAC, switches, sockets, thermostats, alarms, fixed lights, plumbing fixtures, built-in cabinetry and fitted storage; keep major kitchen and laundry appliances, including freestanding refrigerators, ovens, dishwashers, washing machines and dryers. Remove TVs, media devices, artwork, rugs, plants, furniture, freestanding lamps, loose storage, personal objects and decorative accessories, including wall-mounted TVs. Preserve any clearly fixed mounting plate, outlet, cable point, or built-in media panel. Preserve the source property exactly: do not add, remove, move, resize, replace, or redesign walls, ceilings, flooring, doors, doorways, windows, openings, columns, beams, niches, stairs, fireplaces, built-ins, fixed cabinetry, counters, sanitary fixtures, radiators, HVAC, switches, sockets, permanent lighting, or any other fixed property feature. Preserve the exact camera angle, crop, perspective, room dimensions, exterior view, daylight direction, and base lighting. Where removed objects hid a wall or floor, reconstruct only the simplest plausible continuation of directly adjacent visible surfaces. Never invent a door, window, opening, niche, fixture, molding, vent, socket, or architectural detail in an occluded area unless the source clearly supports it. Also remove shadows, reflections, contact darkening, and floor or wall impressions caused by removed furniture, while keeping the room's own lighting, material wear, and permanent shadows unchanged.
production_guardrails.no_furniture_semi_fixed_policy: Semi-fixed policy: keep curtains, blinds, curtain rods and tracks; keep wall-mounted mirrors; keep ceiling fans; keep radiators, HVAC, switches, sockets, thermostats, alarms, fixed lights, plumbing fixtures, built-in cabinetry and fitted storage; keep major kitchen and laundry appliances, including freestanding refrigerators, ovens, dishwashers, washing machines and dryers. Remove TVs, media devices, artwork, rugs, plants, furniture, freestanding lamps, loose storage, personal objects and decorative accessories, including wall-mounted TVs. Preserve any clearly fixed mounting plate, outlet, cable point, or built-in media panel.

product_policies.Decision: Never remodel the source property. Style must come from movable furniture and decor.
Pass the known room type explicitly. Do not ask the model to infer it when the application already knows it.
Both living and dining functions must remain readable; reduce furniture count/scale if the room is compact.
Bed is the primary anchor; avoid full living-room and dining-room setups.
Preserve kitchen and appliances; keep sleeping + compact living zones readable; prioritize small-scale furniture and circulation.

product_policies.Policy: No Furniture: major kitchen/laundry appliances, including freestanding fridge/washer/dryer
No Furniture: TVs/media devices, including wall-mounted TVs
No Furniture: fixed TV mount/outlet/cable point/built-in media panel

product_policies.Decision: KEEP — property accuracy takes priority over perfect emptiness.
Remove shadows, reflections, contact darkening, carpet/floor impressions and wall silhouettes caused by removed furniture; keep room lighting and permanent wear.
Use the simplest plausible continuation of adjacent visible surfaces. Never infer a door/window/niche/fixture without source evidence.

blocks.micro: Room type: combined living-dining room; furnish both zones and keep circulation clear.
blocks.standard: Room type: combined living-dining room. Stage both functions rather than treating the room as a pure living room. Create a clearly readable living zone and a clearly readable dining zone, using appropriately scaled furniture for the available geometry. Keep doors, windows, kitchen access, balcony access, and circulation paths unobstructed. If the room is compact, reduce furniture size or piece count instead of forcing an oversized dining table or seating layout.
blocks.detailed: Room type: combined living-dining room. Preserve two distinct but visually coherent functional zones: one for living and one for dining. Adapt furniture quantity and scale to the actual visible floor area and architecture. The living zone should have a clear primary seating arrangement; the dining zone should have a proportionate dining table and chairs without blocking circulation. Maintain comfortable access to doors, windows, balcony doors, kitchen openings, corridors, and fixed fixtures. Do not reshape the room to fit furniture. In smaller rooms, use fewer, slimmer, or more compact pieces rather than overcrowding.

blocks.micro: Room type: bedroom; prioritize the bed and bedside furniture, avoiding living-room or dining furniture.
blocks.standard: Room type: bedroom. Make the bed the primary functional anchor, with proportionate bedside furniture and only the supporting pieces the available space can comfortably accommodate. Keep circulation around the bed, doors, wardrobes, windows, and fixed fixtures clear. Avoid dining-room furniture and avoid staging the bedroom as a second living room.
blocks.detailed: Room type: bedroom. Use a correctly scaled bed as the main anchor and add proportionate bedside furniture, a rug, and only limited supporting pieces such as a bench, lounge chair, dresser, or lamp when the visible space supports them. Keep access to doors, wardrobes, windows, balconies, and fixed fixtures unobstructed. Do not force a sofa, coffee-table layout, dining table, or unnecessary extra seating into the room. Adapt the composition to the actual room geometry rather than moving or reshaping architectural features.

blocks.micro: Room type: studio; preserve the kitchen, create compact sleeping and living zones, and keep circulation clear.
blocks.standard: Room type: studio apartment combining sleeping, living, and kitchen functions. Preserve the entire existing kitchen and its appliances, counters, cabinetry, and access. Create a clearly readable sleeping zone and a compact living zone using small-scale furniture appropriate to a studio. Place the sleeping zone in the most spatially appropriate available area without obstructing the kitchen, doors, windows, or circulation. Do not overcrowd the room.
blocks.detailed: Room type: studio apartment with integrated sleeping, living, and kitchen functions. Treat the existing kitchen as fixed property: preserve cabinetry, counters, appliances, plumbing fixtures, and access exactly. Create two readable furnished zones outside the kitchen footprint: a sleeping zone and a compact living zone. Use small-scale, multifunctional, or visually light furniture where appropriate. Choose the sleeping position from the actual available geometry rather than imposing a fixed wall. Keep all circulation routes, appliance access, doors, windows, balcony access, and kitchen work areas unobstructed. Do not turn the studio into a pure living room, do not delete the bed function, and do not overcrowd the space.
